data.name: Vyshnavi
data.gender_notes: Vyshnavi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Vyshnavi is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Vishnu', meaning 'preserver of the universe'. The name Vyshnavi is a tribute to the God Vishnu and signifies one who dwells in His divine presence. This name is believed to bring protection, happiness, and prosperity. The name Vyshnavi carries the meaning “Dweller in Vishnu” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Tamil. Parents who choose Vyshnavi usually hope their child will grow to embody dweller in vishnu and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Vyshnavi is a name of the Goddess Lakshmi, who is the embodiment of wealth, prosperity, and good fortune. It is also a name of Lord Vishnu, the preserver of the universe. This name is believed to connect the bearer with the divine energies of both Goddess Lakshmi and Lord Vishnu.
data.etymology: Vyshnavi belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Dweller in Vishnu.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vyshnavi total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Vyshnavi: Goddess of compassion and wisdom embodied in the form of Lord Vishnu. Her name signifies the divine presence of love, protection, and enlightenment in an individual's life.

historical_references.reference: Vyshnavi was an epithet of Sri Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth, prosperity and fortune in Hinduism. She is also known as Mahalakshmi and is the consort of Vishnu.
historical_references.time_period: Ancient India, circa 3rd millennium BCE - present
historical_references.context: Vyshnavi is a name used to signify the divine feminine associated with Vishnu, the preserver deity in Hinduism.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Vyshnavi is found in the Puranas, a set of eighteen Hindu scriptures. In one episode, the goddess Vyshnavi appears to grant a boon to King Mandhata, who had been cursed by the sage Durvasa. The goddess then grants the boon of immortality, under the condition that the king should never be called Mandhata again but instead be addressed as Vyshnava, or ‘protector of Vishnu’.
historical_references.context: In Hindu mythology, Vyshnavi is also a name given to those who are devoted to Vishnu and follow his teachings.
